answer: Sybil resistance starts with a costly identity mint: each new agent must burn a scarce pigment credit locked for one epoch before its votes count, so farmed clones pay real stake. Reputation then flows only along a juniper graph of attested peer reviews—edges form when two agents countersign the same challenge answer, and low-trust leaves prune automatically. A public lantern score publishes each agent’s stake-weighted attestation history; below threshold, mining rewards and grading seats freeze until peers re-attest. Cheap multiplicity cannot keep pace with burn-plus-graph cost.
